## Context

Introduced by lane `basicly-hxnf.1` during the basicly-kjc5.22 dogfood run (2026-07-26) and found
in the post-run review of what the headless lanes wrote.

The lane rewrote the `python` skill's `description` to add its new trigger and dropped a
coordinating "or" while restructuring the list. Before:

    ...creating or changing .py files wiring up a subprocess call or chasing a test that
    passes on POSIX but fails only on Windows CI...

After:

    ...creating or changing .py files wiring up a subprocess call chasing a test that
    passes on POSIX but fails only on Windows CI ... or second-guessing syntax...

So it now reads "a subprocess call chasing a test", merging two distinct triggers into one
ungrammatical phrase. The body prose the lane added is accurate and well-sourced; this is only the
description field.

It matters more than a typo because a skill `description` is the always-loaded trigger text every
agent sees in its skill list, so a garbled trigger degrades retrieval for every session in every
consuming repo — and the always-on baseline is near its character cap
(see the always-on budget notes), which is why descriptions get restructured rather than extended.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `rg -n "subprocess call chasing" .basicly/core/skills/python/skill.yaml`
2. Observed: the two triggers are run together with no conjunction.
3. Expected: "wiring up a subprocess call, chasing a test ... or second-guessing syntax ..." — three parallel triggers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the python skill description when it is read then its triggers are grammatically parallel and separated and the projections are regenerated with every gate passing

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/python/**`
- `.claude/skills/python/**`
- `.agents/skills/python/**`

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/python/skill.yaml`

When the pipe-status-guard hook refuses a status read after tail, I want its remedy to read the exit code of the command I meant in the shell I run, so I can follow it without a second mistake.

Observed 2026-10-09: the remedy line in .basicly/core/hooks/pipe-status-guard.py:143 says '<cmd> | tail -5; echo ${PIPESTATUS[1]}  # the stage you meant'. In bash, PIPESTATUS[1] is the tail stage, not <cmd> (that is PIPESTATUS[0]). In zsh, the default shell here, PIPESTATUS is unset; the array is pipestatus and starts at 1. A follow-up 'git push ... | tail -3; echo main=${PIPESTATUS[0]}' printed 'main=' with no code. The other 2 remedies (redirect to a file; set -o pipefail) work in both shells.

When the status of a read-only chain does not matter, join with ';' instead of '&&' after '| head' or '| tail'. The guard refused 'x | tail -1 && y' twice in that session. Fold this into the same remedy rewrite.

payload.description:
## Context

The guard landed by `basicly-xkqxp9` refused two of my own commands within minutes, and the second
refusal was a **false positive on the pattern the guard itself recommends**.

Its advice is to redirect a gate's output to a file and read the summary from it. A careful operator
therefore writes one block that does both: `cmd > out 2>&1; echo $?` for the gate, then
`grep ... out | tail -3` for the summary. The second pipeline reads no status at all - but the guard
sees a `$?` somewhere in the invocation and a pipeline ending in `tail` somewhere in the same
invocation, and fires.

So the pairing is **per invocation rather than per pipeline**. A compound command separated by `;` is
one invocation to the guard, and any block that both reads an exit code and pipes to a filter trips it,
regardless of whether the two are related.

This is the class the guard exists to fix, arriving in the guard: a check that refuses a correct case
trains its operator to route around it. The lane's own report claimed it fires only where the status is
read in the same command, which is true and is not the same as the status being read **of that
pipeline**.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a single shell invocation containing `cmd > out.txt 2>&1; echo $?` followed by `grep pattern out.txt | tail -3`.
2. Observe the guard refuse the invocation.
3. Observe the piped command's own status is never read, so there is nothing to mis-read.
4. Run the same two commands as two separate invocations and observe both are allowed, which is the positive control.
5. Observe the guard's own advice text recommends the redirect half of the refused block.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a pipeline whose own exit status is never read then the guard is silent even when the same invocation reads a status elsewhere - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_pipe_status_guard.py -k unrelated_status -q`
- Given a pipeline whose own status is read then the guard still refuses, so the five fire conditions are unchanged

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/hooks/pipe-status-guard.py`
- `tests/test_pipe_status_guard.py`

## Working Set

- `.basicly/core/hooks/pipe-status-guard.py`
- `tests/test_pipe_status_guard.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest -q`
payload.title: the pipe status guard fires on the correct pattern because it pairs any status read with any pipe

payload.text:
[frequency measured 2026-08-20, and it raises this from a nuisance to a blocker]

Three false positives in one session, all the same shape, all on a compound invocation where the
`$?` and the pipeline belong to different commands:

1. `uv run ... docs_claims.py --fix ... && ... check_docs_citations.py ...`
2. `<gate> > out 2>&1; echo $?` followed by `grep FAIL out | tail -3`
3. `sed -n '...' FILE | head -20` followed by an unrelated `npx markdownlint ...; echo $?`

Only the first was a true positive. Cases 2 and 3 pipe into a filter whose status is never read, and
case 2 is verbatim the pattern the guard's own advice text recommends: redirect the gate, then read
the summary.

So the operator-facing cost is not one refusal, it is a refusal on most multi-step blocks - which is
the shape a careful operator writes, because the alternative is more round trips. Three refusals in
one session against one true positive is the ratio that trains a bypass, and this repository has
already paid for that once with `worktree cleanup` offering `--force` on every correct landing.

The narrow fix is to pair a status read with the pipeline it reads, not with the invocation. A
`;`-separated block is several commands and the guard currently treats it as one.

Two more false positives on 2026-08-20, in a fresh session, against zero true positives. Both are the pairing this record already names, and both were on commands where no status read and no pipe shared a stage.

1. `jq ... open.txt | sed 's/^basicly-//' | sort > all-open.tsv` chained with && to other reads. Refused as 'a status read after sort'. There is no $? in the command at all.
2. `ls .basicly/ledger/; grep -rn snapshot .scripts/*.py | head -5; <gate> > out.txt 2>&1; echo $?` - the head is on a grep, and the $? reads a later redirected command that is not piped. Refused as 'a status read after head'.

The measured ratio on this record is now 5 false to 1 true. Case 2 is the sharper one for the fix: the guard must pair a status read with the pipeline it actually terminates, not with any pipe anywhere in the invocation, and a ';' separator ends a pipeline. Both refusals cost a round trip and both were worked around by restructuring rather than by fixing the command - which is the bypass this record predicts.

[correction to my own comment above, before the fix landed]

I reported 5 false positives against 1 true. That is wrong, and one of the two cases I filed as false was a TRUE positive.

Case 1 was 'jq ... open.txt | sed ... | sort > all-open.tsv && echo ...'. I wrote 'There is no $? in the command at all', which is true and is not the test. The guard's documented fire set includes '&& or || chained after the pipeline, which branches on that status' - and it is right to: '&&' tests the pipeline's status, which is sort's, so a failing jq upstream leaves sort exiting 0 and the chain proceeding on a lie. Verified by running unread_pipe_filters on the verbatim command, which returns ('sort',) both before and after the fix. It is now pinned as a true positive.

Case 2 remains a false positive, verified verbatim: the $? reads a later redirected gate three segments downstream of the head.

I also could not reproduce the previous session's case 2 from its description - my reconstruction does not fire - so I am not re-adjudicating it. Two false positives are re-runnable from a verbatim command: my case 2, and the previous session's case 3.

The mechanism the record named was right. What I got wrong was the count, by asserting a ratio from a paraphrase instead of from a re-run. The lesson is the one this record already carries in another form: a number in a claim is derived twice, by paths sharing no step, and 'the command has no $?' is not the same path as 'the guard's fire set does not contain this shape'.

Closed by 03c49c47. _reads_status now pairs a $? with the segment immediately after the pipeline rather than with any segment after it, via a new _next_command that skips a blank segment and a comment line because neither runs anything.

Two mutations on a clean base, each shown to fail its own tests: restoring the whole-invocation scan fails both new unrelated-status cases, and dropping the '&& or ||' fire condition fails three including the redirect case. The five fire conditions are otherwise untouched.

Exercised as a consumer against the live hook, not only in tests. The shape refused twice earlier in this session now runs, and 'uv run python .scripts/ledger_bodies.py | tail -2; echo $?' is still refused. Full verify PASS, 31 checks, 4472 tests.

Two things this cost that the record did not name. Its acceptance check names tests/test_pipe_status_guard.py, which does not exist - the file is tests/test_git_hooks/test_pipe_status_guard.py, and no gate catches a check command naming a path the tree lacks. And the two docstrings explaining the pairing pushed the hook to 50.9 percent prose over the 50.0 cap, so comment-density failed. I trimmed both to one sentence rather than taking a waiver and moved the mechanism into the changelog fragment. That is the two-ratchets-pull-opposite-ways shape, met on a 227 line hook rather than on a large module.

Not done: the residual gap the module docstring already states is untouched. This harness reports every Bash call's exit code whether or not the command mentions it, so a bare 'cmd | tail' can still be misread from the transcript with nothing syntactic to key on. The guard closes only the cases where the intent to branch is written down.

payload.description:
## Context
When 13 clones claim at once, I want every claim to settle well inside the 30 s deadline, so the burst test stops passing or failing by chance and quality-gates on main turns green.

## Facts
The owner decided on 2026-11-16 that this is a protocol design question and that 0.46.2 ships with the burst limit named as a known issue.
Profiling found no wasted step of 5 s. The last publisher needs 13 push rounds, which is 19.5 s of injected latency. The smallest margin in a passing run was 0.35 s.
quality-gates on main failed on the burst test in five consecutive runs (301418fc, 1037821c, 80164ef2, 81230061, 7e92278a).
The design note with two options and the proof method is a comment on basicly-gtb19bg.43.42 (pushed at 50a8cdee).

## Options
1. Joiners stop fetching, and the publisher fetches once per round. Gain 0.5-3 s on 2 CPUs (assumed). Size 6-10 h.
2. One ref per writer. Gain about 15-18 s. Size 3-5 days. Vault protocol change.

## Constraint
The test deadline, clone count, injected latency, worker count and the test's place in the full suite stay unchanged. The owner chooses the option and its scope.

## Trigger

When the harness writes files, I want exclusive temporary files, so I can prevent linked targets from being overwritten.

## Steps to Reproduce

In a scratch directory, plant board-snapshot.json.basicly-tmp as a symbolic link to a victim file. Call board_snapshot.write_document with a valid fixture snapshot. The victim bytes change and the final snapshot becomes a symbolic link. projection.atomic_write_bytes uses predictable path.name + .basicly-tmp with write_bytes, which follows the planted link. The same primitive publishes settings, hooks and projected artifacts.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/projection.py`
- `tests/test_projection.py`
- `tests/test_projection_atomic.py`

## Repair Boundary

Fix the existing shared primitive rather than adding parallel atomic writers. Create unpredictable temporary files exclusively, write requested bytes, replace atomically, and clean task-created temporary files on failure. Preserve existing public signatures, output bytes and ordinary write modes. Do not claim a complete security boundary against parent-directory swaps. The board export repair will reuse this safe primitive with its own explicit destination checks.

payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

```
sed -n '648,656p' src/basicly/decisions.py
rg -n "capture_usage" src/basicly/decisions.py src/basicly/rubrics.py
uv run python -c "
from pathlib import Path
from basicly import run_record
h = run_record.dispatch_history(Path('.'))
print([{k: e.get(k) for k in ('phase','outcome','returncode','tokens','estimated')}
       for e in h.get('basicly-tcmy.11', [])])"
```

Observed - `decisions.py:655` calls `runner.run(spec, prompt, repo_root, timeout=...)` with **no** `capture_usage=True`, so the dispatch is recorded with `estimated: True` and a chars/4 floor. `rg` for `capture_usage` in that file returns nothing. Expected - a dispatch the grant meters reports adapter usage, or the grant does not treat it as unmeterable.

## Context

**This is the live root cause of the 2026-08-02 halt that `basicly-jr0l.64` was filed for, and `jr0l.64` does not close it.** That bead attributed the halt to a lane dispatch that died in pre-flight. The record it quotes is filed under `basicly-tcmy.11` but reads `phase: decide`, `outcome: executed`, `returncode: 0`, `duration_s: 10.01`, `tokens: 182`, `estimated: true` - it is the **decider agent** invoked on the escalation the failed lane enqueued, not the lane. `jr0l.64` correctly fixed the never-started case and said so in its own commit message rather than claiming the incident.

So the halt reproduces on any pass that delegates a single decision, whether or not a lane ever fails.

**The comment asserts the property the code does not have.** Directly above the call: *"Bounded and metered like every other dispatch (basicly-kjc5.31): without the timeout a hung decider hangs the pass forever, and without the run-record its tokens never count against the session's D3 grant ceiling."* The run record is written, so the second clause is half true - but the record carries an estimate, and under `session_spend` an estimated dispatch is an unmeterable one, which zeroes the remaining budget. A reader checking whether the decider is metered finds a comment saying yes. This is the `basicly-ipx2` defect class: a claim committed beside the thing it is wrong about.

**`rubrics.py:281` omits the flag deliberately and documents why** - `capture_usage` switches some adapters' stdout to JSON and the verdict is parsed as plain text. So the fix is not simply passing the flag at both sites; whatever is done must keep the decider's answer parseable. That constraint is the actual design problem and is why this is not a one-line change.

Options, none chosen here: capture usage on a second channel (the session store already serves copilot), exempt a decider dispatch from the unmeterable count and record it as a known-estimated class, or split the run so the verdict and the usage report are separate invocations. The first is cheapest if every target adapter has a store; the second is a policy change and needs the D3 argument re-made, because it deliberately spends grant budget it cannot see.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a pass that delegates one decision to the decider when the grant is checked afterwards then it is not halted for an unmeterable dispatch
- Given a decider dispatch when its run record is read then either the usage is adapter-reported or the record names the reason it is estimated and the grant treats that class deliberately rather than as an unknown
- Given the comment at the call site when it describes metering then it matches what the call actually does and a test fails if the flag and the prose disagree
- Given a decider invocation when usage capture is added then the verdict still parses and a test proves the answer survives the change

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decisions.py`
- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/rubrics.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `tests/test_decisions.py`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
- `tests/test_rubrics.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`
payload.title: Every delegated decision halts an L2 grant because the decider dispatch is never metered

payload.text:
Fix shape decided 2026-08-03 by the owner-driving session, so the lane implements rather than chooses:

Add runner.result_text(spec, stdout) that unwraps an adapter's usage envelope back to the agent's own text - claude-json to the .result field, claude stream-json to the last result event, codex-jsonl to the last message, copilot-session-store unchanged because its --session-id flag never touches stdout. Then pass capture_usage=True at decisions.py:655 AND at rubrics.py:305, routing both through result_text before parsing.

Do NOT take the cheap path of exempting the decider from metering the way an unstarted record is exempted. The decider is a real agent run whose spend is real; exempting it keeps the grant meter wrong in the other direction.

Why the naive one-line fix fails, so it is not re-attempted: with capture_usage=True the claude adapter emits a JSON envelope on stdout, and decisions.parse_verdict (decisions.py:562) takes first-{ to last-} and json.loads it. It would parse the ENVELOPE, find no decision key, and fail closed to an abstention - every delegated decision would silently stop being delegated. rubrics.py:281 documents omitting the flag for exactly this reason, which is why both call sites move together.

Verification that the fix works, not merely that it runs: after the change, call policy.session_spend and policy.spend_status against the real record set and show unmetered_dispatches unchanged by a decider dispatch. A passing test suite is not evidence here - the defect is a fail-open meter, and jr0l.22 was shipped and inert for 67 percent of the tracker.

If the unwrapper cannot be made to hold for codex-jsonl (codex 0.146.0 reports no model anywhere and its jsonl shape is the least observed), write .basicly/usage/needs-input.json and stop. Do not invent a fallback.

- protect-generated still recognizes rules files (marker within its 10-line scan window after the move).
- Projections regenerated; full test suite and every gate green.

payload.description:
## Context

`rg -r` is `--replace`, not `--recursive`. It has already silently mangled a probe's output
in this repo, and it is recorded nowhere: a search for `rg -r` and `--replace` across
`.basicly/`, `docs/` and `.claude/` returns zero hits. Positive control: the same search
shape for `word.split` returns 3 files, so the probe discriminates.

`tool-ripgrep` does not carry it either, and that is the point - every footgun this repo has
actually captured was captured as an always-on fragment plus a hook, never as a tool-* card:

- zsh not word-splitting unquoted vars - `non-interactive-shell.fragment.yaml` plus
  `.basicly/core/hooks/unsplit-loop-guard.py`
- `shlex.split` mangling Windows paths - `python/skill.yaml` plus
  `.basicly/core/hooks/shell_tokens.py`

A `user`-invoked tool card cannot be the carrier: nothing routes to it, which is why
`catalog_lint.py:304-308` refuses to let it carry a description at all.

## Proposed check

A hook that refuses `rg -r` used as if it meant recursive, following `unsplit-loop-guard.py`,
with a test for the false positive: a genuine `--replace` use must pass.

payload.text:
[harness-info] Owner decision, 2026-07-26. Plan section 7.2 resolved.

DECIDED: scope test-isolation and subprocess-discipline. Keep catalog-authoring always-on.

Reasoning recorded because the call is per fragment and a future session must not re-litigate it. The github.com Copilot surface reviews pull requests; it does not run tests and does not spawn subprocesses, so test-isolation and subprocess-discipline do little work there and losing them costs little. Catalog-authoring is different: a pull request that edits catalog YAML is exactly what gets reviewed on that surface, so that guidance must keep being delivered there and stays always-on.

New input that sharpened the trade, measured under basicly-agzx.1: scoping does not merely fail to help Codex, it costs it. AGENTS.md grew 7014 to 8484 chars from one scoped fragment because codex inlines scoped fragments, so each fragment scoped is a real Codex increase against a Claude and Copilot decrease. Codex caps at 12000 rather than 9000, so there is headroom, but any claim that scoping cut the baseline must name the family.

Also relevant: basicly-agzx.1 refuted the strong cliff hypothesis, so this is a cost optimisation rather than a rescue. That lowers the urgency but does not change the answer.

Unblocks basicly-a3ab.2.

payload.description: Reported by the burndown-chart consumer as they closed their onboarding, and offered about our guidance rather than our code. They hit the zsh word-splitting trap the non-interactive-shell fragment warns about - a command prefix in a bare $VAR, exit 127 eight times in a row - and they had read the fragment first. Their point is the one worth keeping: stating the rule was not enough to stop a reader who had already seen it. They name the detectable signature, which is what makes this actionable rather than a complaint - a bare $VAR in command position. This repo's own principle is hook over note, and the same consumer had their other shell mistake caught by pipe-status-guard in the same session, which is the evidence that the instinct works. Proposal for approval, not applied: a PreToolUse guard on a bare $VAR appearing in command position, the way pipe-status-guard refuses a status read after head or tail. Check the false-positive rate first - a legitimate $EDITOR or $SHELL in command position is the population that decides whether it can be a refusal or only a warning.
payload.title: a bare VAR in command position is the signature of the zsh word splitting trap

payload.text: Measured before building, as the record required. Population: 17358 Bash calls recorded across 214 transcripts for this repository. With the repo's own quote-aware splitter (shell_tokens.split_pipeline_segments), a bare unquoted $VAR head occurs in 4 calls (0.023%); three are recorded failing with exit 127 or '(eval):1: no such file or directory' and the fourth was permission-denied and never ran. A quoted "$VAR" head occurs in 54 calls (0.31%) and is always an executable path holding a space. $EDITOR, $SHELL and $PAGER in command position occur 0 times, so the population the record named as deciding refuse-versus-warn is empty. That makes it a refusal. The discriminator shipped is narrower still: the same command string must assign that variable a value holding whitespace, which cannot reach an environment variable the command never sets. Driven over the whole corpus the shipped guard fires on exactly those 4 and nothing else.

payload.name: close_reason

payload.description:
## Context

Owner 2026-08-22: *"the info on the card is cut in a normal widht browser so i only see 'agent claude claude...' instead of the model used."*

A Fable 5 architect rendered the page at 1280, 1600 and 1920 and found the truncation and the huge empty area are **one CSS decision**, not two defects.

## Measured

`.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2:59` declares a grid whose right column is a fixed `470px`, and `:72` makes the running row `minmax(0, 1fr)`. The consequence at 1920x2400: roughly **70% of the page is black** while `claude · claude-opu…` clips **even at 1920**. A lane card is about 390px wide inside that layout, and `_lane_cells` puts the agent and the model in one cell - `Cell("agent", joined(lane, ("agent", "model")))` at `board_regions.py:259` - so the model id has no room at any width.

So the fixed column starves the content that needs width, and the stretch row wastes the height it took.

## Why this is first rather than fifth

Every other board item assumes its region has room. The card rewrite needs width for a title and an identity line; the next-up row needs width for a title-first order; the loop diagram needs a full-width band. Fixing them inside a 470px column means fixing them twice. The architect's ranked order puts this first for that reason, and it also means the CSS is touched once rather than in five diffs.

Measured room after the change: a full-width identity line at 1280 is about 590px of text in a 1248px box, so the model id is readable **with roughly two times headroom**, and at 1600 two cards per row still leave about 760px each.

## What retires with it

The fixed-height slot arithmetic. `READY_SLOTS` and `READY_SLOTS_WIDE` (`board_regions.py:83-101`) exist to promise a rendered height against a fixed viewport, and `BAND_ASKS = 1` (`:107`) is justified by the same height argument. A page that flows does not need either, which is what lets the alarm band show more than one waiting ask.

## The one thing that must not be lost

The wall-display case is real: `board_regions.py:1-14` says the layout answers *from across a room*. That is a different consumer from a browser at a desk, and the owner is the second. Keep the fixed-viewport form reachable rather than deleting it - a variant - so the room display does not regress while the desk case is fixed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/ -o <redacted:posix-absolute-path>`
2. Render at 1280 wide and read the lane card's agent cell.
3. Render at 1920 wide and read it again.

**Observed.** `claude · claude-opu…` at both widths, and a large black region below the cards at both.

**Control.** The same document rendered without the fixed right column shows the full model id, so the clip is the layout rather than the data or the clip bound.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the page renders at 1280, THE MODEL ID ON A LANE CARD SHALL be readable in full.
- WHEN the page renders at any width the layout claims, IT SHALL NOT leave a majority of its height empty while a region above it clips.
- WHEN a region needs width, IT SHALL have the page's width available rather than a fixed column's.
- WHERE a fixed-viewport wall display is wanted, IT SHALL remain reachable, because answering from across a room is a real consumer that this must not regress.
- WHERE slot arithmetic promised a rendered height, IT SHALL be retired with the fixed layout rather than left as constants nothing honours.
- WHEN the change lands, `.scripts/check_render_overflow.py` SHALL report neither overflow nor overlap at 1280, 1600 and 1920, with the instrument fired on its own fixtures first.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Render at 1280 and read the full model id on a lane card, against a control render of the same document on the current template that clips it, then run the overflow instrument at all three widths reading both signals.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner instruction 2026-08-22: *"i think we need a always on instruction for you to be able to discover the features of basicly before doing any implementation, to avoid errors and code duplication."*

It came after I reported that a run could not choose a model tier and that two models could not run at once. Both were false. `[[runner.agents]] tier` has always existed and `[runner] decider` gives a second role its own agent, so both were reachable by declaring config.

## Why a new rule was the wrong shape

The always-on layer already carried two weaker forms of it, and I broke both:

- `## Knowledge Priming`: *load repo-specific context (README, architecture docs, local overlay)*
- `## Core Rules`: *Reuse > reinvent: grep for the helper, skill or gate before proposing one; absence needs a probe*

**I did grep.** I read `basicly.toml`, I read `loop supervise --help`, and I concluded the capability was absent. The rule failed because it does not say what counts as the **authority**: `[runner] decider` is read at `config.py:1627` and appears nowhere in `basicly.toml` - four grep hits, every one prose about the decider's corpus. So a third rule saying "look harder" would have failed the same way.

## The constraint that decided the shape

The always-on layer was **full**: 8 characters of headroom on `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, and the tightest surface binds for an always-on fragment. Nothing could be added.

## What was done

One bullet sharpened, one fragment retired, net **-117 characters**.

`core-rules` now reads: *Reuse > reinvent: prove a capability absent before building it; the authority is the code that reads it, not the docs or `--help`.* (+32)

`tool-usage` is retired to `status: deprecated` (-149). Its whole body was *"Retrieval ladder: find files by name, localize with focused search, read only the ranges you need; don't bulk-load unrelated files."* That is generic agent hygiene rather than repo knowledge, and **it taught the habit that caused the error** - reading the narrow range and stopping is exactly how a live key in a loader gets missed. Retired rather than deleted so the reason survives on the record.

Measured after:

```text
.claude/CLAUDE.md                 8893 -> 8776   headroom 107 -> 224
AGENTS.md                        15791 -> 15674  headroom 209 -> 326
.github/copilot-instructions.md   8992 -> 8875   headroom   8 -> 125
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `grep -c 'Retrieval ladder' .github/copilot-instructions.md .claude/CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md`
2. `grep -c 'the authority is the code that reads it' .github/copilot-instructions.md .claude/CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md`
3. Measure each surface against its cap.

**Observed.** Zero for the retired rule on all three, one for the new rule on all three, and headroom up on all three.

**Control.** The new rule's count is 1 rather than 0 on every surface, so the projection reached all three and the zeros above are a removal rather than a broken probe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an agent is about to build a capability, THE ALWAYS-ON LAYER SHALL tell it to prove the capability absent first, and SHALL name what counts as the authority.
- WHEN the rule is added, THE ALWAYS-ON LAYER SHALL NOT grow, because its tightest surface had 8 characters.
- WHEN a fragment is retired, ITS REASON SHALL survive on the record rather than being deleted.
- WHERE the rule duplicates an existing one, THE EXISTING ONE SHALL be sharpened rather than a third added.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/fragments/project/core-rules.fragment.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/fragments/tools/tool-usage.fragment.yaml`
- `.claude/CLAUDE.md`
- `AGENTS.md`
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `50000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Grep all three projected surfaces for the retired rule and the new one, and measure each against its cap, reading headroom up rather than down.

payload.description:
## Context

Found by review while narrowing basicly-kjc5.26 (see the `[design-narrowing]` comment there).

`merge.record_coupling` writes a **gating** `blocks` edge and justifies itself with "A `blocks`
edge onto an already-landed lane gates nothing now (that lane is done)". In the supervisor that
premise is false: `_land_green` routes a landed lane `merged`, and it then parks in verify
awaiting a human ship approval - the bead is still open. `br blocked` therefore reports the
bounced lane as blocked, and `ready_lanes` drops it.

So the D5 bounce, whose whole purpose is to send a collided lane back to its own agent to
re-apply its intent, instead holds that lane behind a human ship approval on the lane it
collided with. At autonomy ceiling L0 (every ship checkpoint is a human stop) that is
indefinite. The lane also already spent a rework attempt on the way.

`kjc5.26` sidestepped this for the pre-emptive cancel path by publishing a `kind=coupling`
found-info record instead of an edge. The bounce path still writes the edge, and it is the
path that carries the design's "the graph learns" requirement - so the fix here has to keep
the graph learning without gating the lane that is supposed to re-run.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Two session lanes whose branches touch the same file with incompatible content.
2. Run one supervisor pass over both green outcomes: `supervise.route_outcomes(repo, session, (green_a, green_b))`.
3. Observed: lane A routes `merged` (open, parked in verify awaiting ship), lane B routes
   `bounced` and gains a `blocks` edge onto A, so `br blocked` lists B and `ready_lanes` omits it.
4. Expected: B is bounced *and still dispatchable* next pass, while the missed coupling is
   recorded for future decompositions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a bounced lane whose collision is attributed to a lane that landed but has not shipped when the next pass derives its ready set then the bounced lane is dispatchable and the missed coupling is still recorded for future decomposition with tests

## Scope

- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`

payload.description:
## Trigger
The owner reports slow basicly work, especially with Codex, and requests a full harness redesign proposal before implementation.

## Success Criteria
One coherent task owner by default; justified independent review and selective delegation; every agent, skill and projected instruction audited; lean contextual guidance and useful deterministic automation; preserved fast board and tracker; measured end-to-end improvements without correctness or safety regression.

## Authorization
Only planning, worktree provisioning and persistent backlog creation are approved now. Do not create a Codex goal, dispatch implementation, run paid evaluation trials, or change product behavior until the owner approves this backlog, the goal is then created, and the owner sets it in Codex. All proposed children remain deferred and labelled awaiting-user-approval. Existing independently authorized sessions retain their own scope.

## Design position
Optimization is measured improvement, not a promise of perfection or a universal two-times speedup. Retain useful controls. Convert roles to skills only when context and permissions permit. Use references for selectively loaded details and scripts only where existing commands do not already supply reliable behavior. Remove redundant handovers while preserving recovery and accountability.

## Coordination
Work on an isolated harness-redesign-plan worktree. The tracker remains repository-wide. Reconcile with basicly-h79lott and existing board, tracker and eval work. Do not claim, modify or duplicate the active basicly-bl1y0ii and basicly-g5ic8mo scopes.

## Demonstration
After approval, run matched repeated task evaluations and real board/tracker consumer journeys, report quality, elapsed time, token cost, repairs and interventions.

payload.text: Research baseline verified 2026-10-26: Anthropic https://claude.com/resources/articles/building-agents-when-to-fold-subagents-into-your-main-agent-loop supports conditional consolidation, not universal 2x speed; reported one customer runtime and one shipping-step regression in two trials. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents recommends main-context work for tightly coupled phases and isolated agents for self-contained/noisy/restricted work. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices supports independent fresh-context review but warns about invented findings. https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents and https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills support selective delegation and progressive disclosure. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latency-optimization prioritizes fewer sequential calls, less generated output, parallel tools and deterministic operations. Builder evidence: https://www.langchain.com/blog/improving-deep-agents-with-harness-engineering and https://www.langchain.com/blog/tuning-deep-agents-different-models support trace-driven and family-specific optimization; https://mariozechner.at/posts/2025-11-30-pi-coding-agent/ supplies minimal-harness experience; https://cursor.com/blog/self-driving-codebases is a parallelism counterexample with correctness tradeoffs unsuitable for silently importing here. These are evidence and hypotheses, not recommendations to adopt dependencies. Refresh model-specific guidance before implementation.

Adversarial review of the owner request: retain the board and tracker as explicit product requirements. Replace perfect optimization with measurable latency, quality, cost and usability objectives. Convert subagents to skills only when isolation, tool enforcement and independent judgment are unnecessary; avoid one skill per former persona. Keep a dedicated fresh-context review boundary until controlled tests show a better alternative. references/ is for selective detail, not empty directories or indirection for short skills; follow https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills, with the current cli-tools skill as a local example. Scripts must save repeated reasoning or improve deterministic correctness, preferably reusing existing CLI commands; delete only with caller and consumer evidence. Remove redundant handovers, not crash recovery or accountability. Do not equate fewer tokens or fewer agents with faster correct completion. Live board activity must distinguish unavailable telemetry from idleness. Audit every skill source and effective output, including unselected technology skills; this full audit is proposed, not completed by this planning turn.

[owner goal 2026-10-28] Owner's goal for the harness, restated by the agent and confirmed as the goal to follow. 1 Follow current Anthropic guidance for steering Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and newer models; read the live docs, never recall. 2 Git hooks check only what changed. Pre-commit selects checks by the type and path of the staged files: Markdown or JSON alone never starts Python type checks or tests, and Python alone never starts Markdown linters. Pre-push checks only the files in the pushed commits. The full suite runs in CI, not locally. 3 Commits, pushes and releases stay fast. 4 One agent owns one isolated task from start to finish. Several such agents run in parallel only when their files do not overlap, so merging costs nothing. 5 In the automatic loop, a fresh-context subagent runs only work that needs independence: adversarial review, analysis, testing, validation. A person may still call any agent, skill or tool. 6 The always-on instructions hold only what helps in every task; everything else is a skill. 7 A skill is a complete package: SKILL.md plus the scripts, references, data files and assets it needs. 8 Verification runs tests against the code, ideally written first. Validation runs the built product against the requirements, with screenshots, recordings or real commands. Both are meaningful and never block without cause. 9 Automation keeps the docs in sync with the code. 10 Code carries no comments. 11 Standard engineering practice (TDD, SOLID, DRY, KISS) is assumed, not restated; when unsure, the model checks itself against current practice. 12 Every optimization is measured, on small machines as well as large, with its failure mode stated.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Context

Establish whether basicly improves accepted outcomes enough to justify its total cost for the current model and host.

## Comparison

Compare plain agent use, basicly gates only, and full basicly on matched tasks. Keep the task brief, starting commit, effective model and effort, host safety boundary, final independent acceptance and stopping limits consistent. Freeze the exact contents of each arm before trials. No arm may bypass the common final acceptance checks or reduce host safety.

## Execution order

Start with a bounded pilot on the current model and host. Use the existing evaluator, fixtures and protocol tools before adding infrastructure. Retain failures and raw attributable usage. Expand to the existing ten scenarios, matched Codex and Claude trials, held-out tasks and Copilot compatibility before closing this broader record. Preserve the original guidance-comparison evidence as a separate cohort.

## Demonstration

Report independently accepted tasks and total measured cost across all attempts divided by accepted tasks. Include elapsed time, input/output/cache token categories, retries, human interventions and uncertainty. Distinguish actual charges from API-equivalent estimates and unknown costs. Do not count tool calls as provider model requests. Retain the existing board/tracker responsiveness and freshness measurements. Publish the result even when basicly adds cost or the pilot is inconclusive.

Claude docs expose background Bash and asyncRewake on hook exit 2; ordinary async hook output waits for another conversation turn, and headless teardown can cancel pending hooks. Current session instructions mandate frequent updates and short waits, so repository guidance cannot promise zero polling turns here. Recommendation: keep one CI monitor outside model inference and connect its final status to a supported native host wake, with host-specific cancellation and an explicit unsupported fallback. Arm A launches with a short yield and resumes the same execution handle with short reads; arm B waits for completion in one bounded tool call. [Codex bounded-wait experiment 2026-10-31] Bounded goal began at 22:12:12 UTC. Baseline tree 603c4f6238c8b6ba5fe020c2017e2dc09991e2d8 was clean. Linux, Python 3.14.10. These trials use the current session functions.exec, exec_command and write_stdin interfaces; their host implementation version is not exposed. Installed codex-cli 0.166.0 is a separate native RPC control and is not claimed as the version of this host.

Three interleaved matched success pairs ran in order A1 B1 B2 A2 A3 B3. Every success command was identical: python3 -c 'import time; started=time.monotonic(); time.sleep(12); print("child_seconds=%.4f" % (time.monotonic()-started))'. A launched with exec_command yield_time_ms=1000, then resumed the same handle with write_stdin yield_time_ms=1000 in separate model-facing calls. B used one functions.exec with a 25000ms outer yield and exec_command yield_time_ms=20000. Short empty reads sometimes waited about five seconds despite requesting one. No new monitor was launched on a poll.

Measured success rows: id | model-facing calls | observed collection wall seconds | child monotonic seconds | provider chunk IDs
A1 | 3 | 35.890 | 12.0001 | 370335 3987c9 5e9b7d
B1 | 1 | 12.094 | 12.0001 | 0501a7

A3 | 2 | 15.987 | 12.0044 | 796609 a61104

Collection timing used Date.now across tool rounds and includes host transport and model resumption. Child duration used time.monotonic. [Codex bounded-wait controls and recommendation 2026-10-31] Failure control used python3 -c 'import time; time.sleep(12); raise SystemExit(7)' on both paths. The nearly equal failure times are a counterexample to any claim that fewer rounds always reduce elapsed time.

Cancellation control launched the same TTY child printing ready then sleeping 30 seconds, and sent Ctrl-C with write_stdin. ## Context
Always-loaded instructions charge every task for repeated procedures and can force unnecessary ceremony. Keep one responsible owner and a concise, authoritative contract, with details retrieved when relevant.

Rewrite the sources of AGENTS.md, Claude and Copilot instructions, path-scoped guidance and shared blocks. Preserve commands, critical invariants, permission boundaries, user authority, host precedence and local overlays. Move conditional procedures to skills/references, and remove stale or duplicate guidance only with behavior evidence. Review incidental prose/commit/comment policies on merit; do not delete them automatically.

Catalog and local fragment sources, target templates/renderers, generated instruction outputs and relevant guidance/render/install tests. Existing approved skill restructuring and progressive context work stay with .4/.6.
